_about: Inputs to the dashboard's 'New Mac' tabs. NOTHING here was measured on this machine or on the proposed ones: every figure is published by someone else, estimated by a third party, or (where kind is 'derived') worked out from other published figures. Read by dashboard/bench/loader.py.

max128.label: Max-128
max128.name: M5 Max, 128 GB
max128.usable_basis: assumption: ~78% of RAM, the share oMLX allows one model on the 256 GB machine (~200 GB)

ultra256.label: Ultra-256
ultra256.name: M5 Ultra, 256 GB
ultra256.usable_basis: oMLX allows ~200 GB for one model (MacStories)

swe_bench_pro_note: BenchLM leaderboard; setups differ between vendors, so small gaps are directional. Scores are the vendor/leaderboard configuration, not a 4-bit build on the machine in question. OpenAI's July 2026 audit estimated ~30% of the public split is broken.

max128.why: ~68 GB at moderate context; peak 155 GB at 256K, so long contexts will not fit in 128 GB

max128.note: decode: LLMCheck's estimate for Q4. Community oMLX submissions on M5 Max 128 GB (MTP build, 128K ctx) range from 5 to 86 tok/s decode, so treat as wide-ranging; the top 10 are 76-86. prefill: median of those top-10 submissions (987-2,402), not a controlled measurement

ultra256.why: 187 GB peak; oMLX refused to load 8-bit in one test and macOS killed a 6-bit run at 177 GB

max128.why: 8-bit or BF16 fits in 96 GB (MacStories tier table)

ultra256.note: 6K prompt (MacStories); Tom's Hardware and Ars Technica report 46-50 decode

max128.note: decode: LLMCheck's estimate for Q4; prefill: derived as the Ultra figure x 40/80 GPU cores, found in no source

max128.why: memory use was not reported on any machine

ultra256.why: MacStories says it fits 256 GB in MLX 4/8-bit

candidates.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash (4-bit; 2-bit via ds4 on Max)

max128.why: 4-bit (~155 GB) does not fit; antirez's ds4 2-bit build is ~98 GB, which is a quality cost. A Reddit user says larger builds crashed their 128 GB machine

ultra256.why: ~155 GB at 4-bit (~187 GB at NVFP4 in another source)

max128.note: one Reddit user's report for the 2-bit ds4 build (27-30 decode; prefill 340 at empty context, ~275 at 100K); a second user saw ~30. Anecdote, not a benchmark

max128.why: a Reddit user runs the iq3_s GGUF with 256K context on a 128 GB MacBook; no size reported. BenchLM lists the model as proprietary, which conflicts with that GGUF existing, and the score is for the vendor's full-precision model

ultra256.why: no size reported; presumably fits since it runs on 128 GB

max128.why: ~96 GB at 4-bit (from research notes), leaving little room for context
~92 GB at Q5_K_XL per a Reddit user, leaving ~8 GB of usable memory for context
Q4_K_M ~52 GB, Q8_0 ~85 GB per a Reddit user who runs it on a 128 GB machine

ultra256.why: one source says it still fits in 256 GB; another puts it in the 512 GB tier

today.name: M1 Max, 64 GB (measured here)
today.note: Quality is the published full-precision SWE-bench Pro score for the model; speed is our own measurement of the 4-/8-bit build. gpt-oss-20b and Apple's model have no SWE-bench Pro score.

claude.note: Quality: SWE-bench Pro (BenchLM; Haiku 5.5 from CodingFleet). Speed: Artificial Analysis output tokens/s at the highest reasoning effort it lists, so they include thinking tokens. No prefill figures exist for hosted models, and the time-to-first-token values on those pages (12-560 s) look like reasoning time rather than latency, so they are left out.

code.note: LiveCodeBench v6 as reported by Alibaba; token budget unknown, so not comparable with our 4k/16k runs
